startup.name: Asakana
startup.one_liner: Automating away manual admin for food distributors: texts to ERP
startup.description: Restaurants send orders to food distributors by email, text, and photo. Someone at the distributor retypes every one of them into the ERP. Asakana does that entry instead: orders land in the ERP already entered, and anything unclear goes to a person before it goes in. Live at US seafood distributors today, returning 40%+ of order-desk time to selling. Founded by a seafood distributor and a Gemini builder.

yc_acceptance.basis: Assumed accepted in this test, so this is a note. The published rate is about 1 percent of over 10,000 applicants (references/yc_acceptance.md). A team of four with a seafood distributor founder, a live product at US distributors and a stated 40 percent time saving gives a lift, offset by many AI order entry companies applying in 2025 to 2026.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC could pass because AI order entry for distributors is a well known idea with funded rivals such as Choco, and several earlier YC companies have the same pitch. The claimed 40 percent time savings is unverified and the niche of seafood could be too small.

killers.evidence: Choco and several YC companies sell AI order entry to distributors.
killers.mitigation: Own the seafood niche and expand from there, with deep ERP integrations.

killers.risk: ERP vendors add order intake themselves
killers.evidence: ERP and EDI vendors can build email and photo order capture inside their systems.
killers.mitigation: Integrate with many ERPs and become the neutral layer.

killers.evidence: Seafood distribution is a narrow slice of food distribution, limiting early revenue.
killers.mitigation: Expand to adjacent proteins and produce distributors.

killers.risk: Accuracy and trust in order entry
killers.evidence: Errors in orders cost distributors money, so reliability must be very high; the design sends unclear cases to people.
killers.mitigation: Publish accuracy rates and keep a human in the loop.

technical_complexity.rationale: Parsing email, text and photo orders with models and writing them to ERPs is feasible for a small team. ERP integrations and handling messy product catalogs take work, but are not research problems.

takeover_risk.rationale: Rivals have funds and distribution and can add order capture within months. A domain founder and live deployments provide a lead but it is narrow.

evidence.claim: Distributors employ order desk staff who retype orders, a measured cost that automation can cut.
Funded vendors such as Choco sell AI order intake, so there is a market that pays.

roadmap.proof: Three paying distributors and a measured 40 percent time saving.

brand.name: Asakana
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Asakana" --era 2022+ returned invented_or_proper, 1 word, 4 syllables.
strengths: Sounds like sakana, Japanese for fish, which fits seafood
weaknesses: Narrow tie to seafood may limit
brand.rationale: The name echoes fish in Japanese, a neat fit for the starting niche, but it may feel narrow if the company expands to other foods. Like many invented YC names it works if the product wins.

narrative.headline: A domain insider with live customers in a crowded AI order entry category; seed is likely, later rounds depend on beating funded rivals.
narrative.general_summary: Asakana has the strongest early signals among order entry teams in the batch: a founder from seafood distribution and live use at US distributors. The category is crowded with funded and YC rivals, so each later round is about average for B2B. The likely path is a small to normal seed and then a contest for the Series A. It is a forecast from the input file and the base rates only, with no knowledge of what happened after the batch started, and the numbers should be read with wide error bars because the cohorts for these categories are small.

assumptions: Seed means a round above $500K within 12 months of 2026-10-05.
Claims in the description are the company's own.
Analogs from 2025 and 2026 batches are used only for their description, not their funding as evidence.
